parsed.main_gap: Pigeonhole in Section 5 uses only the 2^{n+1}-2 proper nonempty subset sums, giving gap ≤ 1/(2^{n+1}-3), not the claimed d = 1/(2^{n+1}-1).

errors.description: Section 5, eq. (11): with 2^{n+1}-2 values in (0,1) there are 2^{n+1}-3 gaps summing to less than 1, so the minimal gap is only bounded by 1/(2^{n+1}-3) > d. The claimed bound d does not follow as written. (Repairable in one line by also including the empty and full subsets, since the case 'A or B empty' is already treated.)
errors.quote:
They lie in $(0,1)$, so their $2^{n+1}-3$ consecutive gaps sum to less than $1$. When put in nondecreasing order, two consecutive subset sums therefore differ by at most
\[
\frac1{2^{n+1}-1}=d. \tag{11}
\]

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1)-1} is correct and both directions are essentially complete: the greedy/alternating-discrepancy lemma, the pairing characterisation, the tree-component/powers-of-two lower bound, and the refinement-based upper bound all check out. Only the pigeonhole count is off, and the fix is immediate.
